native_resolution: 30 m EPSG:32629 grid of the terrain strata for heights, 10 m WorldCover cells for land cover, samples every 30 m

units.distance: m along the line from its first point

valley_floor_rule: contiguous samples around the lowest sample with elevation at most 2200 m, the upper limit of the published valley floor (1800 to 2200 m, SCI-19)

tabant_meridian.label: Cross-valley section along the meridian through Tabant
tabant_meridian.rule: The meridian (line of constant longitude) through Tabant, clipped to the frozen polygon: the part that contains it, from its northernmost to its southernmost point; distance runs from north to south.

valley_axis.label: Long profile from the outlet to the head along the longest flow path of the drainage network
valley_axis.rule: The longest flow path of the drainage network from the outlet to a head: at each confluence the upstream segment with the longer way up, ties by the larger upstream area and then the lower segment number; distance runs from the outlet.

strata_band_agreement.note: The strata raster gives each 10 m cell the band of its 30 m cell; the profile gives the band of the sample's own interpolated height.

limitations: A profile is read from a 30 m surface model: trees, buildings, steep walls and radar artefacts distort it, and narrow gorges such as the lower gorge near the outlet are not resolved. Heights are metres above the EGM2008 geoid with the DEM's stated vertical accuracy (Copernicus DEM Product Handbook 5.0).
Samples are 30 m apart, so a band crossing or a land cover boundary is placed to within about 15 m, and a feature narrower than 30 m can fall between samples.
Land cover is ESA WorldCover 2021 at 10 m, a single 2021 map applied to the line: tree cover on the valley floor may include orchards, and no class is a pasture, agdal or management unit.
An elevation band is a stratum that organises sampling, cut from the elevation distribution of the catchment; it is not a vegetation type, a grazing zone or a management boundary.
The valley floor segment follows the published elevation range of the valley floor (1800 to 2200 m, SCI-19); it is not a measured flat bottom.

The valley axis is the longest flow path of a D8 network, which follows the main river, not the centre line of the valley; its profile inherits the limits of the drainage network, including places where the surface rises along the line.
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.
